title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

reading.body:
This is a fraud carried out through impersonation, with a generative model used to fabricate the face and voice of a public figure on a live video call. The synthetic likeness was the entry point, not the payload: the money moved through ordinary payment requests framed as fees, exchange charges, a PIN unlock, and a fine. The AI component did its work at the moment of first contact, establishing enough apparent authority for the target to keep paying.

The failure sits at the point of identity verification in a consumer communication channel. Nothing in the call flow required the caller to prove he was the person he appeared to be, and nothing in the payment flow flagged a sequence of escalating demands to a private individual. Catching this would have required either a verification step on the caller's identity or a check on the payment pattern, and neither was present.

What is not established is who operated the deepfake, whether the impersonation of the CBI officer involved any synthetic media at all, and whether any arrest or recovery followed the case registered under the Information Technology Act.

reports.title: ‘CM Vijay’ WhatsApp call promises Rs 11 lakh aid, Bengaluru man loses Rs 1 lakh

summary:
A 29-year-old security guard in Bengaluru named Ratikanta Giri received a WhatsApp video call on September 9 from someone using an AI-generated deepfake to pose as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay. The caller offered him Rs 11 lakh in financial aid and said a manager would arrange the transfer. Giri was then told Rs 5 lakh had been allotted to him and was asked to pay fees, including Rs 5,000 as exchange charges and Rs 18,000 to unlock a PIN.

A person claiming to be a CBI officer then demanded over Rs 50,000 as a fine. Giri paid over Rs 1.04 lakh in total before refusing a further Rs 50,000 demand and realizing he had been cheated. He contacted the cybercrime helpline and Byappanahalli police, who registered a case under the Information Technology Act.
